questions.q: A game show has 100 doors: 1 hides a car, 99 hide goats. You pick one door. The host, who knows what's behind each door, then opens 98 of the remaining doors, all revealing goats, leaving your door and exactly one other closed. If you switch to that other door, what is your probability of winning the car?
Which is true: is 0.999... (repeating forever) less than 1, or does it equal 1 exactly?
choices: It depends on how far the 9s repeat

questions.q: A family has two children. At least one of them is a boy born on a Tuesday. What is the probability that both children are boys? (Assume gender and birth day are each independent and uniformly random, with 7 equally likely days of the week.)
Which is more likely: rolling at least one 6 in four rolls of a fair die, or rolling at least one double-six in twenty-four rolls of a pair of fair dice?
choices: At least one 6 in four rolls of a die
At least one double-six in twenty-four rolls of two dice
